① OBSERVED (designer's friction log #20): "Contributions are additive only. Work running in parallel (the commit overlapped with the rule delta; freshness paths that run side by side) cannot be expressed. Workaround: set the overlapped part to 0 with a note, and accept that the freshness total overstates." The case: a 50 ms write budget whose path is gateway 5 → router 2 → host 6 → then commit 20 running alongside the rule delta 13, which is 33 ms in truth and 46 ms as a sum. Expected: a total that honours overlap. NOT affected: additive quantities (mass, cost, area), where the sum is the truth.

② PRECEDENT, searched in reflow2 and flo2: cap:budget ("Sum contributions along the thread", verified); commit 4f4d0f8 "BL-9 + BL-11 … budgets that cannot lie", which added worst_path; chg:bl58-silent-failure-batch (the provable-overrun verdict). No prior report of a parallel-branch overstatement. Nothing in flo2's design.

③ CANDIDATES: (a) SCHEMA — contributions are one number per node, so overlap cannot be expressed (the reporter's reading). (b) THE OBSERVATION IS WRONG — a path rollup exists and was not found. (c) READER — the path rollup exists, but the verdict does not read it. (d) GRANULARITY, not in the component suspected — the overlapping phases (commit, rule delta) are phases of one operation, not separate nodes, so no contributor structure can hold them.

④ DISCRIMINATORS: (b) and (c) both predict a worst_path in budget_report. (c) alone predicts the verdict ignores it. (d) predicts the designer's case needs contributors that are not nodes.

⑤ MEASURED on 0.74.0, isolated scratch store. Five Components with DEPENDS_ON gw→router→host→store and host→rules, contributions 5/2/6/20/13 ms, and a 40 ms maximum. budget_report returned worst_path [gw, router, host, store], worst_path_total 33.0, path_note "worst dependency path by stated contribution", AND total 46.0, verdict `exceeded`. In code, budget.rs builds worst_path by DAG longest path over DEPENDS_ON (and consumer→provider contracts), but the verdict match compares `total` with the limit. ⇒ (b) HOLDS for the computation: serial-sum and parallel-max IS computed. (c) HOLDS: the verdict reads only the sum, so a correctly modelled latency budget reads `exceeded` when its path is within. (d) HOLDS in part: the designer's phases lived inside components, so they would have needed one component per phase to use the path.
Why the designer did not find the path half: the `constrains` description (which the designer read) never mentions DEPENDS_ON or paths. Only budget_report's own description names "the worst dependency path".

⑥ CLASS: a computation holds two rollups and gates on one without the constrained quantity saying which is its truth. The rule for how a quantity composes is implicit in the code (sum) instead of declared on the Constraint. Would a declared composition have stopped this report? Yes. With `along the path` declared, the verdict reads 33 and the workaround of zeroing a part is unnecessary.

⑦/⑧ OWED, NOT DONE: a pinning test that a maximum budget whose contributors form a DAG with parallel branches returns a verdict consistent with its declared composition (fails today: `exceeded` at 46 when the path is 33), then the fix. How the Constraint declares its composition is an open idea: dec:idea-a-constraint-says-how-its-quantity-composes.
